title: Beyond the 956: Dolly Parton, country music icon, dies at 80
excerpt: Dolly Parton, the country music icon behind “Jolene,” “I Will Always Love You,” and “9 to 5,” died August 25, 2026, at the age of 80 in Nashville, Tennessee, after a brief battle with cancer.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Dolly Parton, the country music icon whose songs “Jolene,” “I Will Always Love You,” and “9 to 5” became part of American life, died August 25, 2026, at the age of 80.

Parton died peacefully in Nashville, Tennessee, at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center, surrounded by loved ones, after a brief battle with cancer, her family announced on August 25. Her publicist, Marcel Pariseau, said in a statement: “After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones.” The announcement was shared in a video message from her nephew, Bryan Seaver.

Born Dolly Rebecca Parton on January 19, 1946, in Locust Ridge, Tennessee, she rose from a log cabin in the Tennessee mountains to become one of the most beloved entertainers in the world — a singer, songwriter, actress, author, and philanthropist whose career spanned more than six decades.

Parton wrote and recorded some of the most enduring songs in country music, including “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You,” and starred in the hit film 9 to 5 (1980), for which she wrote the title song. She was a member of the Grand Ole Opry and the Country Music Hall of Fame, and she founded Dollywood, the theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, and the Imagination Library, the book-gifting program that has put books into the hands of children around the world.

She was laid to rest beside her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Thomas Dean, who died in March 2025 at the age of 82. In lieu of flowers, the family asked for donations to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library.

Rest in Peace, Dolly Parton.

Sources: The Associated Press; PEOPLE; dollyparton.com (official announcement, August 25, 2026).
